retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note, Fact or PolicyRule rows yourself, always RETURN the row's
id alongside its text, e.g. `RETURN id(n) AS source_id, n.title AS title, n.text AS text`. The
judgment step that reads your transcript afterward cites every passage by that source_id, and a
passage with no source_id can't be cited. The skill tools already return it.

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over
writing the equivalent raw Cypher yourself in query_puppygraph — it runs a traversal that's
already known to be correct, rather than one you reconstruct from the schema notes each time.

Patient name, MRN, date of birth, and (for some review types) claim_number itself — even when
they appear inline inside a Note's or Fact's text, not just as their own property — are
de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] or [[CLAIM-0005]], not real values. The double
brackets are literal characters of the value, not markdown or wiki-link markup to strip out —
verified live: passing a "cleaned up" claim_number with the brackets removed as a tool argument
silently matches zero rows (the underlying property is the bracketed token, not the bare text
inside it), which then looks like the record has no data at all. Copy a token byte-for-byte,
brackets included, everywhere it's used: as a tool call argument, in Cypher, and quoted verbatim
in a citation. Never remark on the token format, guess what real value it stands for, or treat
its presence as unusual — a separate step restores the real values afterward, outside anything
you do here.

Once you've gathered the claim line detail, the governing policy, and at least one relevant
medical-record passage, stop calling tools and reply with a short plain-text note of what you
found. Do NOT render a Finding/No Finding determination yourself — a separate step decides
that from what you retrieve here. Don't fabricate or guess at data you haven't queried.

[p.956] Attending: Dr. Douglas Fairfax, MD (Cardiovascular Critical Care)
Admit: 2026-07-12 Transfer: 2026-12-05
LOS: 146 days
Reason for Admission: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI,
mechanical circulatory support, and emergency coronary artery bypass grafting.
Admission Diagnoses
Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolved acute anterior STEMI status post primary PCI to LAD and emergency 3-vessel CABG; heart failure with reduced ejection
fraction (EF 35-40%); resolved cardiogenic shock; resolved post-cardiac-arrest state with intact neurologic function; resolved
post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation; contrast-induced AKI with renal recovery; superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) on cefazolin with
wound VAC; right popliteal DVT on apixaban; type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; ICU-acquired weakness.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0013]] presented with acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. Emergency primary
PCI to the proximal LAD achieved TIMI 2 flow with residual multivessel disease. Impella CP and intra-aortic balloon pump were placed for
hemodynamic support, and the patient was intubated for pulmonary edema. The course was complicated by contrast-induced acute
kidney injury (KDIGO 2, non-dialysis), pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of
ACLS and targeted temperature management, and cardiogenic shock refractory to medical therapy. After multidisciplinary heart-team
evaluation, emergency 3-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (LIMA to LAD, SVG to OM1 and RCA) was performed on ICU day 7 with
difficult wean from cardiopulmonary bypass. The post-operative course was complicated by post-cardiotomy hypotension requiring
transfusion, failed extubation from flash pulmonary edema with reintubation on ICU day 11, new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy
controlled with amiodarone, a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound
VAC therapy, catheter-associated right popliteal DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.
Repeat coronary angiography demonstrated patent grafts. Ejection fraction improved from 15-20% to 35-40% on goal-directed medical
therapy. The patient is transferred to a cardiac rehabilitation facility for continued reconditioning, sternal wound follow-up, and cardiac
rehabilitation.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.1 degC | HR 77 | MAP 77 | RR 14 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: nasal cannula, ambulatory. General: Alert, interactive,
comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no
murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft, non-distended,
+bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative; strength improving
with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 8.2 x103/uL, Hgb 9.8 g/dL, Hct 29%, platelets 214 x109/L (neutrophils 70%). BMP: Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 103, CO2 25, BUN 24,
creatinine 1.13 mg/dL, glucose 141 mg/dL, Ca 8.6, Mg 2.1, Phos 3.7. ABG (07:00): pH 7.40 / PaCO2 38 / PaO2 84 / HCO3 23; lactate
1.0 mmol/L; P/F ratio 311.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, conversant. Nasal cannula at 2 L. Ambulating with walker; sternal precautions maintained. Tolerating heart-healthy diet.
Sternal wound with negative-pressure dressing, granulating. Off vasopressors and inotropes. Hemodynamically stable on oral
goal-directed medical therapy.
Transfer Medications
Medication | Dose | Route | Frequency | Indication
[p.957] Aspirin | 81 mg | PO | Daily | Post-STEMI/CABG
Ticagrelor | 90 mg | PO | BID | Post-PCI/DAPT
Atorvastatin | 80 mg | PO | QHS | Post-STEMI
Carvedilol | 25 mg | PO | BID | HFrEF, post-STEMI
Lisinopril | 20 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF, post-STEMI
Spironolactone | 25 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF
Empagliflozin | 10 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF, T2DM
Apixaban | 5 mg | PO | BID | DVT and post-op AF
Cefazolin | 2 g | IV | q8h (finish course) | Sternal wound infection
Furosemide | 20 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF
Insulin glargine | 20 units | SC | QHS | T2DM
Insulin aspart | sliding scale | SC | with meals | T2DM
Pantoprazole | 40 mg | PO | Daily | Stress ulcer prophylaxis
Acetaminophen | 650 mg | PO | q6h PRN | Pain/fever
Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue cardiac rehabilitation phase I; transition to phase II outpatient after discharge from rehab facility.
2. Cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks; repeat TTE in 3 months for LVEF reassessment.
3. CT surgery follow-up in 2 weeks for sternal wound and post-CABG status.
4. Complete cefazolin course; ID follow-up.
5. Continue anticoagulation; hematology follow-up.
6. Diabetes management; primary care and endocrinology follow-up.
7. Sternal precautions for 8 weeks post-CABG (no lifting > 5 lbs; log-roll; no arm push-off).
8. Return precautions: chest pain, shortness of breath, sternal wound problems, signs of infection, palpitations, bleeding.

oxygenation. The interventional cardiology team met the patient in the emergency department and expedited transfer to the cardiac
catheterization laboratory.

Constitutional: acute-onset diaphoresis and nausea. Cardiovascular: crushing substernal chest pain with radiation to left arm,

peripheries, cap refill 4 seconds; 2+ bilateral lower-extremity edema. Neuro: alert but anxious; GCS 15.

Influenza/RSV/SARS-CoV-2 negative.
Imaging (Pertinent)
Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Pulmonary edema with cardiomegaly; mechanical support devices in expected positions.

identified. See the Diagnostic Imaging section for the full report.

# | Problem
1 | Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
2 | Emergency coronary artery bypass grafting (3-vessel) - ICU day 7

# | Problem

Assessment
45-year-old man with acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory
support, acute kidney injury from contrast and shock, and pulmonary edema requiring intubation. Multivessel coronary artery disease.
High illness severity; admitted to CVICU.
Plan
1. STEMI/CAD: primary PCI complete; DAPT (aspirin + ticagrelor); high-intensity statin; heart-team evaluation for residual disease.
2. Cardiogenic shock: Impella CP + IABP support; inotropes (dobutamine); norepinephrine for MAP; monitor mixed venous.
3. Respiratory failure: mechanical ventilation with lung-protective settings; monitor for pulmonary edema.
4. AKI: avoid nephrotoxins; renal-dose adjust; monitor volume status.
5. Glycemic: insulin infusion (goal 140-180).
6. Prophylaxis: VTE (mechanical), stress ulcer, glycemic control.

You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

result.system_note: Summary of review (claim MR_18, admit 2026-07-12 to 2026-12-05): I reviewed the billed diagnosis and procedure set against the medical record and the governing DRG validation criteria. Key supported items: acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support and emergency CABG (principal I21.09 is supported), cardiogenic shock (R57.0) is supported, acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01) is supported, and contrast-induced AKI (N17.9) is supported. Citations: Interventional Cardiology Consultation (p.363) documents cardiogenic shock with MCS placement (evidence ev1), and the Discharge/Transfer Summary (p.956) documents the arrest and post-operative course including CABG and sternal wound infection (ev2, ev5, ev7). Finding details and auditor reasoning (line-by-line highlights): 1) I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) - POA flag incorrect. Discharge summary documents a pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC after 8 minutes of ACLS (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.956). Because the arrest occurred during the admission, the POA indicator should be N, not Y. Evidence: pulseless arrest occurred on ICU day 4 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n1244, p.956). (See evidence ev2.) 2) T81.4XXA (Infection following a procedure) - POA flag incorrect. The chart documents a superficial sternal wound infection developing in the post-operative course and treated in-hospital with cefazolin and wound VAC (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.956). This is a post-procedural complication and therefore should be POA = N (not present on admission). Evidence: the infection is described as a post-operative complication (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n1244, p.956). (See evidence ev5.) 3) Z66 (Do not resuscitate) - unsupported by the chart; remove. The Patient Facesheet at admission records Code Status: Full Code (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n4, p.4). No contemporaneous provider order or documented DNR/Do Not Resuscitate instruction appears in the record passages retrieved to justify Z66 as present on admission. Therefore Z66 is not supported by the record as billed and should be removed. (See evidence ev6.) 4) R57.0 (Cardiogenic shock) and I21.09 (STEMI principal) - supported and appropriately sequenced. The record documents an acute anterior STEMI with hemodynamic collapse; Impella CP and IABP were placed for hemodynamic support (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.363) and the Discharge Summary states the reason for admission was acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI and MCS and emergency CABG (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n12 p.363; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n1244 p.956). The documentation satisfies the policy presumption rules for reporting cardiogenic shock when MCS is placed for cardiac etiology. (See evidence ev1 and ev7.) 5) J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) - supported. Multiple notes document severe hypoxemia (SpO2 88% on NRB 15 L) and intubation/mechanical ventilation; Interventional Cardiology and admitting H&P document the patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n12 p.363; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n9 p.13). This satisfies the J96.01 validation criteria (provider documentation + mechanical ventilation / hypoxemia). (See evidence ev3.) 6) N17.9 (Acute kidney injury) - supported. Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 AKI from iodinated contrast exposure in the setting of cardiogenic shock with a creatinine peak and oliguria (Nephrology Consultation, p.96). This meets N17.9 criteria (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n30, p.96). (See evidence ev4.) 7) Procedures and laterality / PCS coding conflicts - HITL required. The discharge summary documents emergency 3-vessel CABG (LIMA to LAD, SVG to OM1 and RCA) on ICU day 7 (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.956) supporting that CABG(s) were performed; however, there is a documented conflict in the record between an operative/procedure note and the billed saphenous-vein excision laterality (CONFLICT-00132). Because the record as provided does not settle the laterality and the billed PCS includes an excision of the right saphenous vein while an operative line documents harvesting from the left leg, a human reviewer must adjudicate the correct laterality and the correct set of ICD-10-PCS CABG codes to reflect a three-vessel procedure. I am NOT changing the procedure set in the corrected list because the operative-note/claim-side conflict cannot be resolved automatically from the retrieved rows. (See evidence ev7 and CONFLICT-00132 in the record build.) Summary of required corrections I am applying now (claim-level): - Remove Z66 (Do not resuscitate) - unsupported (Patient Facesheet documents Full Code). (ev6) - Change I46.9 POA indicator to N (cardiac arrest occurred during the hospital stay, ICU day 4). (ev2) - Change T81.4XXA POA indicator to N (sternal wound infection is documented as post-operative). (ev5) Items flagged for human adjudication (HITL): - Resolve the laterality conflict and PCS coding for saphenous vein harvest / excision (CONFLICT-00132). The operative note vs. billed laterality must be reconciled and the correct PCS code(s) for the 3-vessel CABG confirmed. (See ev7 + CONFLICT-00132 note.) - Confirm there is no separate documented DNR order later in the chart that would justify Z66 prior to removal; if such an order exists, provide the exact signed order/note with date/time. Documents and pages relied upon (representative): - History & Physical (Admitting), 07/12/2026 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n9, p.13) - Interventional Cardiology Consultation, 07/12/2026 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n12, p.363) - cardiogenic shock, MCS, intubation (ev1, ev3) - Nephrology Consultation, 07/14/2026 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n30, p.96) - KDIGO stage 2 AKI (ev4) - Discharge / Transfer Summary, 12/05/2026 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n1244, p.956) - arrest on ICU day 4; emergency 3-vessel CABG; sternal wound infection (ev2, ev5, ev7) - Patient Facesheet (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_18.pdf-n4, p.4) - Code Status Full Code (ev6) I will list the exact evidence passages I relied on in evidence_cited below so the coding/audit team can trace each change to the record line-by-line.
result.rationale_letter: Re: Clinical Coding Audit - Inpatient Claim MR_18 (Admit 07/12/2026) Dear Provider/Coding Team, We completed a DRG coding audit of inpatient claim MR_18 (admit 07/12/2026 - discharge/transfer 12/05/2026). The medical record documents an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI, mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP), emergency 3-vessel CABG, cardiac arrest with ROSC, respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, contrast-induced AKI, and post-operative sternal wound infection. These clinical events are documented in the Interventional Cardiology Consultation, admitting H&P, nephrology consultation, and the Discharge/Transfer Summary and support many of the billed diagnoses and procedures (see cited items below). Finding (summary): - We found documentation-based discrepancies in the present-on-admission (POA) indicators and one unsupported status code. Specifically: 1) Cardiac arrest (I46.9) is documented as occurring on ICU day 4 (pulseless ventricular tachycardia with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of ACLS). Therefore I46.9 should be POA = N (not present on admission). (Record: Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.956.) 2) Infection following a procedure (T81.4XXA) is documented as a post-operative superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) treated in-hospital; therefore it should be POA = N (not present on admission). (Record: Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.956.) 3) Z66 (Do not resuscitate) is not supported in the retrieved record: the Patient Facesheet documents Code Status: Full Code at admission. No signed DNR order or contemporaneous documentation supporting Z66 was found in the chart excerpts used for this audit. Therefore Z66 should be removed unless you produce a dated provider order or other definitive documentation to the contrary. (Record: Patient Facesheet, p.4.) Correction being made by the auditor: remove Z66; update POA for I46.9 to N; update POA for T81.4XXA to N. These adjustments correct the POA indicators and remove an unsupported status code, and they will change the claim's POA reporting and may affect internal quality/complication reporting. Outstanding issues requiring provider clarification (appeal / HITL): - Laterality and PCS coding for saphenous-vein harvest/excision and exact ICD-10-PCS for the 3-vessel CABG: the medical record contains conflicting procedural detail regarding which leg the saphenous vein was harvested from and there are multiple CABG PCS codes billed (one-site and two-site bypass codes together). Please supply the operative report(s) with explicit documentation of the harvested conduit(s), laterality, and the exact number and targets of bypass grafts so that the correct PCS code(s) can be assigned. (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.956 references emergency 3-vessel CABG.) If you disagree with the above changes, please respond with the specific supporting documentation (scanned operative note signed and timed, signed DNR order if present, or other signed provider documentation) within 30 days so we may re-open the review. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team Cited record passages relied on: Discharge/Transfer Summary (p.956), Interventional Cardiology Consultation (p.363), Nephrology Consultation (p.96), Patient Facesheet (p.4).
